target_customer: New car shoppers (free or paid per quote), monetized from dealers
problem: Buying a new car meant haggling with several dealerships; CarWoo had dealers compete on quotes without pressure.
business_model: Marketplace: dealer fees and a small buyer fee (a $19 quote fee was reported in 2010)

founders.name: Tommy McClung
founders.background_notes: Later joined TrueCar as VP of product; later co-founded AxleAuto

exit.reason: Could not secure the additional capital (reported need of at least $50M); closed 20 January 2014 and its assets went to TrueCar.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web marketplace with dealer lead routing; the hard part was dealer supply, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Dealer relationships gave some two sided effect, but TrueCar and others served the same dealers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TrueCar absorbed CarWoo's assets and hired nine of about 40 employees in January 2014.

market_need_then: Car buyers disliked dealership negotiation, and the company reported over 5,000 dealers by February 2011 and 13,000 by July 2012, which indicates dealer demand for leads.

branding.domain_note: Used carwoo.com; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful, stress free tone with an exclamation mark in the name

brand_strength.rationale: Playful memorable name but no press about the brand was found; a USPTO word mark filing for CARWOO! is shown as cancelled in 2009.

outcome_analysis: CarWoo raised a Series A in 2010 and grew its dealer network, but in 2013 its CEO sought at least $50M more to keep pace and could not close it. It shut down in January 2014 and its assets, plus nine staff including the CEO, went to TrueCar, the larger competitor. A February 2014 Inc retrospective reportedly also cited a costly acquisition and supply issues but was seen only in summary.
notes: Series A amount conflicts: Xconomy headline says $4.2M in October 2010, other coverage says about $6M, Seedtable says $4.5M; CB Insights says $10.82M over 6 rounds. A further $6M round in December 2011 (total over $12M) is from one snippet and unverified. Founding year varies (2008, 2009, 2010). Competition list limited to TrueCar from 2011 coverage; no 2009 to 2010 sources found. Inactive status agrees with shutdown, assets acquired. TrueCar was named as the main rival only in 2011 coverage (TechCrunch, 2011-02-03), so it is not listed as a dated competitor.
